parsed.current_inefficiency: cook time, steep duration and lime alkalinity set empirically; over/under-cooking shifts texture, niacin release and dough quality, with manual experiential control
parsed.ai_technique: in-line NIR (near-infrared) spectroscopy + gradient-boosted regression (XGBoost) for soft-sensor endpoint prediction
parsed.how_it_improves: A fiber-optic NIR probe immersed in the steep tank streams 900-1700 nm absorbance spectra of the cooking maize/nejayote every few seconds; an XGBoost regressor trained on spectra labeled with offline lab measurements (degree of gelatinization/DSC, pericarp removal %, moisture, bound niacin) predicts these quality variables in real time. The model outputs a live 'cook-doneness' index and predicted minutes-to-endpoint, which drives a controller to cut heat and start the wash exactly at target -> eliminates over/under-cooking batch variance, cuts energy and steep time, and stabilizes downstream masa quality without destructive sampling.
parsed.why_not_done_before: Nixtamalization is dominated by small/artisanal and mid-size tortilla producers with thin R&D budgets; building the labeled spectral-to-quality calibration dataset requires pairing an industrial NIR rig with DSC/HPLC niacin assays across maize varieties, and the caustic, hot, particulate-laden lime steep is a hostile probe environment, so no one has fused process-NIR with boosted-tree soft sensors here.
parsed.primary_quote: Cooking time and steeping (minutes to ~a day) and alkalinity are set empirically

reasoning_trace.reasoning: The core inefficiency is an unmeasured, empirically-set endpoint for an opaque chemical cook. NIR is a mature, food-industry-proven probe for moisture/starch/protein state and works through slurries; XGBoost soft sensors are standard in process industries for spectra->property mapping. Fusing them as an in-line endpoint predictor is concrete and buildable. I rejected pure computer-vision hull-detection (only sees surface, misses gelatinization/niacin chemistry) and generic 'IoT temperature control' (alkalinity/starch state, not temperature, is the missing signal).
reasoning_trace.decision: in-line NIR spectroscopy with XGBoost soft-sensor predicting gelatinization, hull removal and niacin to control cook/steep endpoint
reasoning_trace.confidence: medium - NIR+boosted-tree soft sensors are proven elsewhere, but the calibration dataset and caustic-probe ruggedization are real lift
